children: By George Glover, Mariapaula Gonzalez, Ty Roush, and Connor Smith
Stocks soared Wednesday after Democrats won control of the House and the Senate, removing the risk of political uncertainty. Some of the year's top AI plays took a hit.

SpaceX and Tesla were pressured as the stocks dropped 3.8% and 3.3%, respectively. Elon Musk had spent almost half a billion dollars on trying to prevent Democratic victories in the U.S. midterm elections.

Defense stocks also struggled. RTX slid 2.6% and Lockheed Martin declined 6.9% as investors bet the Democrats would scupper President Donald Trump's bid for a $1.5 trillion boost to military spending.
The blue wave in Congress also sparked a selloff for Trump Media & Technology, which tumbled 25% to $4.49.

Advanced Micro Devices rose 1%. The semiconductor maker's third-quarter earnings came in well above Wall Street's expectations, but the stock's gain was likely held back by fears over what the Democrat sweep means for the AI trade. Super Micro Computer fell 5.7%, even after reporting strong first-quarter earnings. Micron dropped 7%.
CVS Health sank 13%. Investors remained focused on a federal program update that created something of a cliffhanger during the last quarterly call.
Novo Nordisk climbed 5%. The Danish drugmaker raised its full-year earnings outlook, as third-quarter sales of its Wegovy weight-loss pill came in well above Wall Street's expectations.
Bloom Energy dropped 6.4%, The company bypasses the power grid by using fuel cell-based onsite power, which CEO KR Sridhar said can benefit from the backlash over AI data centers.

Datadog fell 14%. Investors looked past a beat in revenue and earnings estimates for the third quarter. Morgan Stanley analysts have questioned whether Datadog can sustain growth of around 30% into 2027.
Uber Technologies rose 4.9% after reporting better-than-expected third-quarter earnings, thanks to its fast-growing delivery business.
Amdocs plunged 30% on an escalating dispute with T-Mobile, which weighed on the company's revenue outlook.
Block surged 15%. The Square and Cash App owner beat analysts' third-quarter earnings targets and bolstered its full-year outlook as an AI-powered transformation plan takes hold.

McDonald's gained 6.5%. A drop in foot traffic contributed to a 0.2% dip in U.S. comparable sales in the third quarter. Investors, however, appeared to cash in on hopes for the company's new growth strategy.
